title: Hazel and the Deadline
premise: Mara Fairweather built her career on being forgettable—a private security contractor whose clients pay her to be invisible and whose past is a carefully maintained fiction. When a stranger named Ivo Kessler arrives claiming she once saved his life, Mara knows it's a lie, but the 'interest' he demands is real: extract his sister Lena, a cryptographer defecting from the syndicate Mara's own agency secretly protects. As Mara runs the extraction, she realizes Lena is bait in a trap designed to flush out the agency's mole—Mara herself, or whoever they believe she is. Forced to choose between the found family she's assembled and the ghost identity she's been hiding, Mara burns her cover to expose the mole, saves Lena, and finally stops running—claiming a name and a place she never thought she deserved.
about_author: Bram Sterling is the pen name of a former logistics coordinator who spent a decade moving people and cargo through the gray zones of Eastern Europe before turning to fiction. Sterling writes lean, propulsive thrillers about people whose loyalties are their last remaining currency.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. We meet Mara mid-job, protecting a paranoid financier who trusts no one, least of all her. Her routine—packed bag, polished cover story, zero attachments—is established with quiet precision. When she returns to her apartment and finds a stranger sitting in her dark kitchen, the beat is cold dread: her invisibility has been breached.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, flashback-tinged. Ivo Kessler spins a story of a favor she never performed—a rescue in Tallinn she has no memory of. He doesn't want money; he wants her skills, to extract his sister Lena from a syndicate safehouse in Riga. The emotional beat is dissonance: the lie is flawless, which means someone built it for her specifically.

chapters.title: Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Alternating Mara and Ivo POVs. Mara investigates Kessler and finds his records end three years ago—same year her own cover was manufactured. Her handler, Deverell, warns her off with unusual urgency, which only sharpens her suspicion that her own agency is entangled. The beat is the first crack of doubt in everything she trusts.

chapters.title: Riga Rules
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She takes the job anyway, assembling her scrappy crew—fixer Tomas and comms whiz Priya, the closest thing she has to family. Recon of the safehouse reveals Lena Kessler is guarded too well for a mere defector; she's being showcased. The beat is rising unease dressed as professional confidence.

chapters.title: The Defector's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, first appearance. Inside the safehouse, Lena has already figured out she's bait and is playing a longer game of her own—copying ledgers that implicate the syndicate's partners, including a Western security firm. She engineers a partial escape to force the timeline. The beat is fierce agency: the prize is also a player.

chapters.title: Extraction, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The extraction goes nearly clean until Mara spots the ambush signature—it matches her own agency's playbook. She aborts, saving Lena but burning Ivo's trust. Lena, handcuffed to a radiator in a safe flat, coolly tells Mara she knows who Mara really is. The beat is vertigo: the hunter realizes she's the quarry.

chapters.title: What Mara Buried
chapters.summary: Mara's POV with intercut memory. Lena forces the truth into the open: Mara's fabricated past was built by the agency to plant her as the perfect fall guy for the syndicate's ledger. Deverell calls, ordering her to deliver Lena—confirming everything. The beat is grief and fury: her whole life was a setup, and her crew is now in the blast radius.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Alternating Mara, Lena, and Priya POVs. The crew goes dark, moving through Riga's port district while agency hunters and syndicate cleaners converge. Ivo reappears, revealing his real role: he built Mara's cover years ago and has been waiting for her to be activated. The beat is found family forged under fire—trust chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Climax at the Riga freight terminal: Mara trades herself to Deverell to buy Lena's escape route, then flips the trap—streaming the syndicate ledger live as Deverell confesses the frame job, letting the syndicate's partners and the agency destroy each other. The beat is white-hot sacrifice turned checkmate.

chapters.title: A Name of Her Own
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, weeks later. The mole is exposed, Deverell gone, the syndicate bleeding. Mara, presumed dead by her old employers, chooses to stay that way—keeping Tomas, Priya, Lena, and even Ivo as her real family. She unpacks the go-bag at last. The beat is quiet belonging: the woman built to be invisible finally lets herself be seen.
